label: Segmented Control
title: Segmented Control
summary: Use a Segmented Control to switch between two to five short, exclusive options, such as Daily, Weekly and Monthly.
corePrinciple: One choice from a short set, always in view.

anatomy.title: A track of equal segments
anatomy.description: A lavender track holds the options side by side. The selected one fills purple with a white label; the others are labels on the track.
blocks: Rounded lavender background that holds the segments and fills its container.
An option people can tap; its label sits on the track.
One or two short words, centred.
Purple fill and a white label mark the current choice.

configuration.title: Two to five options
configuration.description: Set the options and the one that starts selected. Every segment gets the same width, so the number of options decides how much room each label has.
blocks: Opposites, such as Buy and Sell, each take half the track.
The usual case: a period or a view with three choices.
Five is the most that fits: on a 360 px phone each segment is about 59 px.

states.title: Selected, unselected, and pressed
states.description: One segment is always selected. A pressed segment dims until release, then becomes the selection. There is no disabled or loading state.
blocks: The purple fill moves to the segment you tap; Enter, Space, and the arrow keys do the same from the keyboard.

sizing.title: Full width, 43 px tall, equal segments
sizing.description: The track fills its container and splits it equally, with 8 px between segments and no padding of its own. Each segment is 43 px tall: 12 px above and below a 19 px label, with 16 px at each side. A label that doesn’t fit ends in an ellipsis, and the track never runs past its column. In a row, the track is as wide as its labels need, 304 px for Daily, Weekly, and Monthly, and a narrower row ends them in an ellipsis.
blocks: In a 216 px column each segment is about 66 px, too narrow for any of these labels, so each ends in an ellipsis. Daily, Weekly, and Monthly need about 300 px.

content.title: One or two words per option
content.description: Labels share the width equally and end in an ellipsis when they don’t fit, so keep them short and parallel: Daily, Weekly, Monthly. Use the words people see in the content below, and select the likeliest option first.

inContext.title: Switching a portfolio’s period
inContext.description: The control sits above the numbers it changes. The screen keeps the selected period and updates the value below; the control only reports the tap.

doDont.description: Each pair shows a control people can read at a glance versus one that breaks its own layout.

sources.title: Use the public Segmented Control contract
sources.description: The guide compares the Figma component with the installed package and its Storybook stories.
blocks: Installed jfs-components is 0.1.78 (27 October build) from the team’s private package repository. Figma’s Segmented Control is one 393 × 43 component whose slot holds the segments; the package matches its colours, its 43 px height, and its equal widths. Labels that don’t fit end in an ellipsis. On the web the control is a tab list: the selected segment is announced as selected and is the only one in the Tab order, and Enter, Space, and the arrow keys select. Dark mode shows the same colours as Light, so this page shows Light only. The published Storybook predates the current stories.
